# Conservation of Nose-Touch Avoidance Across *C. elegans* and Relatives

Five of the six species we tested avoid nose touch much the same way (Figure 5A). *C. tripartitum* is the exception. Its avoidance rate dropped below 10% after the first few positive trials, so it adapts to the stimulus faster than *C. elegans* and the rest (Figure 5A). In the first three trials, though, it responded much like *C. elegans* (Figure S2 in Additional file 2).

We ablated the ASH neurons in the five nose-touch responsive species, and avoidance disappeared (Figure 5A). Four of the five still responded in 20–30% of trials (Figure 5A). *Caenorhabditis* sp. 3 did not: its ASH-ablated animals lost the response entirely (Figure 5A).

The AWC neuron, by contrast, plays no part. Ablating it left the nose-touch response intact in every species (Figure S3 in Additional file 2).

UPO-06: PrhI Gene Synthesis
UPO-06 carries the coding sequence for *Ralstonia solanacearum* prhI, the ECF sigma factor you need for transcription driven by the Prh signal transduction system. PrhR activates the gene, which then directs sigma factor expression by switching on the PprhJ promoter. We optimized the sequence for expression in *Escherichia coli*.

UPO-11: PprhJ Promoter Synthesis
UPO-11 gives you the PprhJ promoter region. It responds to plant cell contact through signal transduction mediated by PrhA and PrhR, and PrhI activates it. Like UPO-06, it's optimized for expression in *Escherichia coli*.

Subject: Key Findings on foxl2 Expression Patterns in Trout

Dear Customer,

Here's what we found about foxl2 transcript expression in your study.

Both foxl2 transcripts showed up very early in development (Figure 2). foxl2a was highly restricted in the male. foxl2b, the diverged paralog, was present in most adult extragonadal tissues we examined (see Additional file 2).

In adult females, foxl2b sat almost entirely in the skin, gill, and ovary. In the testis, though, foxl2b expression was very strong. That matches earlier findings: foxl2b present, foxl2a absent, in later stages of testis development in trout [23].

Put together, these results suggest foxl2b may regulate male-specific genes (such as cyp19b1), particularly later in development.

Now the head. Its dorsum is strongly longitudinally rugose, with 5–7 rugae between the frontal carinae at eye-level. The rugae are irregular and meander slightly, usually with a few anastomoses. The dorsal alitrunk is finely but strongly reticulate-rugose throughout, with broad, shining interspaces. The petiole dorsum is rugulose; the postpetiole ranges from rugulose to only faintly sculptured. The gaster is unsculptured. We derived a time-dependent mild-slope equation, following the formal derivation of Smith & Sprinks (1975). From that starting point we obtained the higher-order dispersion relation for waves over an uneven bottom.

Here is what matters most: using only the linear dispersion for steady waves, we recovered equation (2.12) of Chamberlain & Porter (1995), the Modified Mild-Slope Equation (MMSE). To the leading-order solution, the modified curvature terms of the MMSE have significant effects. The slope square terms stay negligible, as the mild-slope assumption requires. So we kept every modified curvature term the MSE drops, and that gave us a uniform model.

To test it, we built a numerical model with the finite element method (FEM) that predicts wave scattering by a varying bottom. In general, the uniform model predicts the salient features of waves over various sea beds, including sinusoidal beds and man-made bars. On sinusoidal beds, it matches the experimental data more closely than other established models. On man-made bars, both the MMSE and the uniform model match the data more closely than the results of Kirby (1986).

One more thing worth your attention: the FEM model also applies to the transformation of waves over arbitrarily-varying bathymetry.

Additionality evaluates the counterfactual: what would have occurred under the status quo had the REC not been purchased or contracted. Without verified proof of additionality, RECs cannot be treated as genuine emissions offsets.

MapleStory Monsters: A Survival Guide to the Underworld

Welcome to MapleStory. Thousands of monsters roam this world, so here's where they live and how to survive them.

The weak monsters: These are the ones you'll find by towns. They wander aimlessly, and you can bump right into them without consequence. If one hits you, just take the damage and move on.

The dangerous ones: The lethal monsters live deep in dungeons.

The aggro mechanic: This one matters. Monsters usually wander aimlessly, even if you bump into them. But if you attack or cast a debuff on an enemy, you "aggro" it. You get its attention, and it comes after you.

Behavioral pattern: Most enemies attack by running into you, over and over.

The best strategy: Against these persistent attackers, just keep hitting them. Your attacks usually have enough knockback to keep them in place.

Dodge tactics: When that isn't enough, jump over them to dodge their attacks entirely.

For the full list, see the MapleStory/Monsters/Complete list.

One last thing: aggro is a two-way street. Stay safe and keep attacking.

Here's something worth knowing about how children learn to speak. Most of us pick up spoken language in the first few years of life. If a child can't hear, that child may never learn to speak. Worse, they may never learn to understand speech at all.

The trouble is that a severely hearing-impaired (deaf) child's deficit often goes unnoticed for years. By the time it becomes apparent, communication problems may have already caused issues within the family and hindered social skills. There is one exception: if the child grows up in a Deaf community where sign language replaces spoken language, these challenges can be mitigated (please see our article on Deaf Culture).

That's why many developed countries test a newborn's hearing. The goal is to prevent the inadvertent isolation of a deaf child within a hearing family. Sign language is a full means of communication, but literacy ultimately depends on the ability to understand speech. In the vast majority of written language, the sound of the word is coded in symbols.

Consider what that means. Someone who hears well enough to learn to speak and read keeps that ability even if their hearing later becomes too impaired to hear voices. Someone who never heard well enough to learn to speak is rarely able to read proficiently (see [4]). Most evidence suggests that early identification of hearing impairment is key to ensuring a child with very insensitive hearing learns spoken language effectively. Listening also plays an important role in learning a second language.

The takeaway is simple: early intervention matters. If you have any further questions, please reach out.

Warm regards,

[Your Name/Company]

Transduction is how your nervous system turns physical and chemical signals into neural impulses. It's the basic process of translating stimuli into electrical signals. In sensory transduction, specialized sensory receptors take physical or chemical inputs and convert them into precise electrical impulses that travel to your brain.

Look at the visual system. In your retina, rod and cone cells bridge the physical environment and neural communication. When light strikes these photoreceptors, it changes the shape of the protein rhodopsin. That molecular shift starts a cascade of events that alters the electrochemical gradient of the photoreceptor. The gradient drops, and so do the electrical signals sent to your brain. So more light hitting the photoreceptor results in fewer electrical impulses. That's how your brain decodes the visual world with such precision.

Subject: Tips for Hitchhiking in the Ruhr Area, Germany

Dear Customer,

The Ruhr Area (German: Ruhrgebiet), often just called the Ruhr, is an urban region in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It's a patchwork of former industrial cities: Duisburg, Oberhausen, Bottrop, Mülheim an der Ruhr, Essen, Gelsenkirchen, Bochum, Herne, Hamm, Hagen, Dortmund, Recklinghausen, Unna, and Witten.

About five million people live here. That's far more than Berlin, Hamburg, or Munich. The motorway density is high, but hitchhiking can still be tough, because the network of minor roads is a maze. The motorways that matter are the A1, A2, and A3.

If you plan to hitch here, stay on those primary motorways. The smaller roads will trap you; almost no transit traffic passes through them. Germany is generally a pleasant place for hitchhiking, but the Ruhr Area is by far its most unpleasant part. Hitching inside the Ruhr feels like hitching in a big city like Istanbul. Each city is independent, yet to a traveler they blur into districts of one massive city.

We hope this helps you plan your trip safely and enjoyably.

Best regards,

Mobile Gaming: The Next Evolution of Co-Creation

Mobile internet is changing how stories can pull you in, because electronic games now run on portable, location-aware interfaces. This is the latest stage in a decades-long evolution of electronic games that cast you as a co-author alongside the original designers, more than an avatar in a gameworld.

Location-aware interfaces let you pull places in the physical world into your gameworld, and the other way around. No interactive media has done that before. And beyond giving you a role in worldmaking, mobile games abandon linear narratives in favor of cooperative storytelling that depends on your experience of place.

The "author-player" worldmaking concept is not new. Mobile games, though, push it past the constraints of traditional video games. They extend worldmaking beyond the screen and into the physical world, turning what you see, hear and feel in real places into storytelling tools.

In our essay, we theorize the unique storytelling potential of mobile games while describing our experience trying to realize that potential through the design and implementation of our hybrid-reality game, University of Death.

Here are the key findings from our analysis of lung tissue volume and functional changes.

We calculated total lung tissue volume using the formula: volume of lung tissue = number of voxels × volume of the voxel, provided the compartment considered has a CT number above zero.

The change in functional residual capacity from PEEP withdrawal (ΔFRC) is the difference in total gas volume in the whole lung between the PEEP and ZEEP states. We defined alveolar derecruitment as the difference in gas volume within poorly aerated and nonaerated lung regions between these same conditions.

We also computed the changes in gas volume from PEEP withdrawal in normally aerated lung regions, characterized by CT attenuations between -500 and -900 HU (see Figure 2).

As described in reference [21], we classified the distribution of lost lung aeration for each patient (lung morphology) as diffuse, patchy, or lobar, based on the distribution of CT attenuations at ZEEP.
